_doc: tools/vulncheck.py (SPEC EVL-5). go_targets: module directories govulncheck scans. osv_sources: lockfiles the OSV scan must report (it scans every lockfile; these guard against a scan that reads nothing). skip_paths: the control fixture, scanned only by `vulncheck.py control`, and spikes/, whose Go modules are throwaway experiments that ship nothing (any other go.mod outside go_targets fails the scan). inlined: copies a bundler put in a package's files whose marks give no version, {holder (name@version of the package a lockfile installs), copy (name@version), files (the holder's files that hold it), why (how they were identified)}, or files that copy another installed package's bundle, {holder, bundle (name@version:path), files, why}, which take that bundle's versions and must carry no mark it lacks (#4197); an entry fails once no lockfile installs the holder at that version (#4153), and a file's unversioned bundler mark fails unless a sidecar, notice or entry gives its version. pruned (D-308): paths the guest image build deletes from an installed package because the guest never loads them, {where (the guest's lockfile; OpenClaw's only, as a plan CLI runs unmodified), holder (name@version), path (a directory ending in / or one file, relative to the package, outside node_modules/), why (what shows it is never loaded)}; guest/openclaw/prune.js deletes exactly these or fails the build, the inlined scan does not read them, and an entry that matches no file fails. accepted: one record per accepted vulnerability and package version, {id (ID or alias), issue (an open issue naming that id and recording why), why, package and version (the exact copy it accepts: npm package, Go module, or for an image record only the Debian source package), optional where (Go target, lockfile, "image" for the image's Debian packages, or "image/initrd" for its initrd's, each scanned by `vulncheck.py image` and accepted only in its own tree; an image record accepts only an advisory Debian has not fixed)}.

inlined.why: Unmarked copies the fingerprint check found (#4234): each file holds 43 string literals only acorn's own files hold, and the string "8.16.0" that acorn exports as its version. Every literal is also in acorn 8.14.0 to 8.19.0, and no acorn advisory affects 8.x (GHSA-6chw-6frg-f759 is fixed in 7.1.1).

Unmarked copy (#4234): it carries the version string "11.12.0", and OpenClaw 2026.10.9 pins 11.12.0. The /export-session chat command reads it into an exported HTML page, so it is not pruned. No highlight.js advisory affects 11.x (the latest fix is 10.4.1).

Unmarked copy inside chrome-devtools-mcp's bundled DevTools frontend, which its THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES names only as devtools-frontend (#4234): 98 acorn literals and acorn's version string "8.16.0". No acorn advisory affects 8.x.

The matching literals (15 and 26) are all CSS property names, such as border-block-start-color and scroll-padding-inline-end. They come from DevTools' CSS metadata, which highlight.js's CSS grammar also lists. Neither file holds highlight.js code (no hljs or highlightAuto).

This is the MCP SDK 2.0.0 code that THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and bundled-packages.json name: @modelcontextprotocol/core, server and client 2.0.0. It shares its error strings with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.x, and chrome-devtools-mcp 1.10.1 does not depend on the 1.x sdk.

The matching literals are code and constants that both packages took from elsewhere, not OpenClaw code. Two are zod-to-json-schema code (getRelativePath, which utilsBundle.js.LICENSE names) and a base64 padEnd fragment, which OpenClaw's unminified, unmarked dist/canvas-host/a2ui bundles also inline. One is esbuild's "Cannot add the same private member more than once" helper. The rest are a `new Map([[` fragment, Brave Nightly's macOS bundle id and a MIME type, which OpenClaw's own chrome-executables and mime tables also list.

Unmarked minified copies in the recorder and trace viewer assets (#4234): each holds "Alias resolution is disabled", which yaml 2.8.4 added, and all 44 of its yaml literals are in 2.8.4 to 2.9.1. This entry names 2.8.4, the oldest such version. Every version from 2.8.3 on is fixed for both yaml advisories.

Image package openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (libssl3t64, openssl, openssl-provider-legacy). The flaw is an infinite loop in CMS_encrypt() to an EC certificate whose group order is 1 (OpenSSL advisory 2026-11-10, fixed upstream in 3.5.10). OSV lists no fixed version for Debian 12, 13 or 14 and security.debian.org still serves 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, so no upgrade clears it. libssl3t64 stays: libsystemd-shared, systemd-resolved and libcryptsetup12 link it; purging the openssl CLI or the legacy provider would clear no record, since the flaw is in libssl3t64. Fails again once Debian ships one.
